question.text: This man won the first free Polish election in 1990 after using his leverage as leader of Solidarity to push back Soviet influence at the Roundtable talks.
question.clue: This man mourned his successor in 2010 after that successor died in a Smolensk airport plane crash.

swap.leadin: The firing of Anna Walentynowicz triggered a strike that led to the creation of this group.
swap.text: Name this trade union that grew from the 21 MKS Demands developed at the Gdansk shipyards.
swap.clue: This group helped remove Secretary Kania and Wojciech Jaruzelski from power, and the Gdansk Agreement and the Roundtable Talks eventually led to a leader of this group being elected as Prime Minister in 1989.

question.text: This date titles a Francisco Goya painting showing a firing squad and a group of prisoners. The work depicts a scene during an 1808 invasion.
question.answerHtml: May 3rd (or 5/3; accept The Third of May 1808 or El tres de mayo de 1808 en Madrid)

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the November Uprising.
swap.text: This city in modern-day Poland was annexed by Austria in the wake of the November Uprising, losing its "Free City" status that had been granted by the Congress of Vienna. This city was the capital of Poland before Warsaw.
swap.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

question.leadin: Name these tactics of parliamentary obstructionism.
question.text: In the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, a member of the Sejm ("Say-m") could enact this type of veto by shouting "I do not allow!" This veto contributed to the Commonwealth's downfall.
question.clue: The increasing frequency of this action led to the creation of so-called "confederated" bodies where this action was not allowed.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about winners of the Nobel Peace Prize.
swap.text: The 1983 prize went to Lech Walesa, who founded the trade union Solidarity in this nation. In 1990, he would be elected as this nation's president.
swap.clue: This country was joined with an eastern neighbor in the Union of Lublin.

question.leadin: This group participated in the Round Table Talks.
question.text: Name this trade union formed at Lenin Shipyard in Gdansk in 1980. It opposed the Soviets and Communism and supported workers through social activism and civil resistance.

swap.leadin: You are traveling the European Route of Industrial Heritage.
swap.text: You may encounter the Historic Silver Mine in Tarnowskie Gory, established by Duke John II of Opole and located in this region seized by Frederick the Great in the War of the Austrian Succession.
swap.clue: Frederick the Great's 1740 occupation of this region triggered the War of the Austrian Succession.

question.text: Stanislaus's daughter had married Louis XV, but he was sent to Lorraine by the French. The Spanish and Sardinians sought to undo the Peace of Utrecht, and therefore allied with the French against the Germans and Russians. For 15 points-name this 1733 to 1735 conflict which ended with confirmation of Augustus III's reign.
question.clue: The person who led the Confederation of Dzikow had previously held the job in question under Swedish domination and was the father-in-law of Louis XV.

swap.text: It was founded by Wadyslaw II, who married Jadigwa, and continued through several Sigismunds until the country fell under the rule of the French Valois. For 15 points, name this Polish royal house of the fourteenth through sixteenth centuries.
swap.clue: This dynasty, first established when a certain king married Queen Jadwiga. It held power in a country long united with Poland.

question.leadin: This polity incorporated the Duchy of Livonia into its realm during the Livonian War.
question.text: Name this polity that officially formed following the Union of Lublin. This polity's Golden Liberty gave the liberum veto to all members of the Sejm ("same").
question.answerHtml: Poland–Lithuania [accept either underlined portion; accept Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; accept Grand Duchy of Lithuania]
question.clue: This state lost one-third of its population during the Swedish Deluge, and this union formed after Duke Jogaila ] married Queen Jadwiga ].

swap.leadin: Twentieth-century Poland went through much turbulence.
swap.text: This former Socialist and editor of the newspaper Robotnik organized the Union of Riflemen to rebel against Russian rule during World War I and ruled newly independent as dictator from 1920 to 1922 and 1926 to 1934.
swap.clue: He ruled from 1918 to 1922 as the head of the military and seized power again in 1926, operating through such proxies as Jozef Beck and trying to appease Hitler until his 1935 death.

question.text: The Hussites, desperate for a leader after the death of Hus, offered this grand duke the Bohemian throne. This leader allied with Polish forces to defeat the Teutonic Order at the Battle of Grunwald.
question.clue: This junior partner in the Ostrow ("AW-stroof") Agreement sent his nephew Prince Korybut to rule the Hussites.

swap.leadin: In 1943, the Baedeker Guide published its guide to this place, where a historian noted that a "shed where dozens of corpses lie awaiting burial is particularly popular" among tourists.
swap.text: Name this place, many of whose residents were sent to Treblinka. After an unsuccessful Jewish uprising, this area of the Polish capital was destroyed.
swap.clue: The Armia Krajowa largely failed to aid an insurrection partially led by Mordecai Anielewicz in this place, which was documented in a report named for the SS officer who suppressed it, Jurgen Stroop.

question.leadin: This ruler defeated the Yaroslav the Wise at the Battle of Bug River and his long war with Henry II was ended with the Peace of Bautzen.
question.text: Name this member of the Piast Dynasty that established the Prince's Law and was succeeded by Mieszko II.
question.answerHtml: Bolesław I Chrobry (prompt on “Bolesław”; accept Bolesław the Great; accept Bolesław the Valiant; accept Bolesław the Brave; accept Bolesław Chrobry)
question.clue: This ruler redeemed the corpse of Saint Adalbert for a sack of gold, and was given a supposed copy of the Holy Lance known as St. Maurice's Spear at the Congress of Gniezno.

swap.leadin: Name these periods from medieval Eastern Europe.
swap.text: This 1648 to 1667 period in Poland saw large territorial losses to Russia and Sweden; it ended with the abdication of Jan II and the signing of the Truce of Andrusovo.
swap.clue: Key precipitating factors of this period include the increased power of the nobility due to Sarmatism and Golden Liberty system, and it saw secondary conflicts like the Second Northern War.

question.text: This 1915 battle near Osowiec ("oh-SOH-v'yets") Fortress got its name from the fact that a regiment of Russians, many of whom were coughing up bits of lung after being gassed, successfully surprise-assaulted Germans nearly ten times their number.
question.answerHtml: Attack of the Dead Men [or Ataka Mertvetsov or Kampf der toten Männer; prompt on partial answers]

swap.leadin: It was led by Mordecai Anielewicz, a member of the ZOB.
swap.text: This is what uprising in the spring of 1943, in which the inhabitants of the namesake location in Poland unsuccessfully attempted to resist Nazi mass deportation to Treblinka.
swap.clue: The vast majority of fighters in this conflict were deported to Treblinka in its aftermath.

question.text: This Polish prince converted to Catholicism in order to prevent Polish absorption into the Holy Roman Empire. He also expanded Polish territory to the Baltic Sea.
question.clue: This first duke and Christian ruler of the "Gniezno State" who was a grandfather of Canute the Great and a husband to Dobrawa. The Dagome iudex references this ruler's potential baptismal name.

swap.leadin: Apocryphally, this dynasty came to power after the cruel Prince Popiel II ("POPE-yell the second") was imprisoned and eaten alive by rats and mice.
swap.text: Name this dynasty that succeeded the Popielid dynasty. A history by Gallus Anonymus claims that this dynasty was founded by a namesake wheelwright with an always-full cellar, an ancestor of Boleslaw ("bo-LESS-waff") the Brave.
swap.clue: The semi-legendary namesake of this dynasty was a wheelwright who was legendarily visited by two angels in disguise who blessed his cellar.
